decls.description: What the decision record says about its standing.

checks.description: A validity date and its day number come together (four rules, one per direction).
checks.name: rule_1

checks.description: A decision that applied and was withdrawn names the day it stopped applying.
checks.name: rule_5

decls.description: One decision, as its record states it: what was decided, about which subject, by whom, when, from when and until when it applies, how it stands, and which earlier decisions it replaces.

slots.description: What was decided, in the words of the record.
The matter the decision is about. Decisions that succeed each other share it.
Who took the decision: a person or a body, by the identifier the domain uses for its parties. Open world: a record that names nobody leaves unknown who decided.
The day the decision was taken (knowledge time). Absent while it is proposed.
The first day the decision applies (validity). Often the day it was taken.
The day the decision stops applying; from that day on it does not apply. Absent when the record names no end.
valid_from as the whole number YYYYMMDD, which orders as the calendar does. A stopgap: rules cannot read a date yet, so the rules read this slot. It goes when they can.
valid_until as the whole number YYYYMMDD; the same stopgap as valid_from_day.
The standing the record gives the decision today. Rules take time from the validity days and from supersedes, and check the state against them.
An earlier decision this one replaces, from the day this one takes effect.

An earlier decision this one looked at again. A reassessment replaces nothing: the earlier decision stands as its own record says. A domain's rule reads it to say that a decision was looked at again after one of its grounds stopped standing. Open world: that no record reassesses a decision leaves unknown whether anybody looked at it again.
Why it was decided, in the words of the record. Text, and no rule reads it.
A principle the decision rests on: what makes it right (the warrant of an explanation). Open world: a record that names no principle leaves unknown what the decision rests on. No rule reads it.
Who answers for the decision today, by the identifier the domain uses for its parties. Not the decider: the one who keeps it and is asked about it. Open world, and no rule reads it.
The day the decision is looked at again. Absent when the record names none.

decls.description: One decision rests on another: its record names the other decision as a ground. A link, named by its two ends (S27), and its source is the record that names the ground. It says nothing about time: whether the ground stands on a reference date is read from the other decision (in_force_on).

slots.description: The decision whose record names the ground.
The decision it rests on.

decls.description: Something a decision serves, and for whom: the purpose of an explanation. One row per thing served.

slots.description: The decision that serves it.
What is served, in the words of the record.
Who is served, by the identifier the domain uses for its parties. Open world: a record that names nobody leaves unknown for whom.

decls.description: A statement that makes decisions right: the warrant of an explanation. A decision names the principles it rests on (Decision.warrant). A principle has no state of its own: it stands as the decision that adopted it stands.

slots.description: The principle, in the words of its record.

The decision that adopted the principle. Its state, decider and validity are the principle's. Open world: a principle whose record names no decision is of unknown standing, never of no standing. A pack whose rules read a principle's standing makes this slot required for its own principles.

decls.description: An option that was weighed for a decision and rejected.

slots.description: The decision that rejected it.
The alternative, in the words of the record.
Why it was rejected, in the words of the record. Text, and no rule reads it.

decls.description: Something a decision leaves out, in the words of its record: where what was decided does not hold. An exception that is itself decided separately is a Decision of its own.

slots.description: The decision that makes the exception.
What is excepted, in the words of the record.

decls.description: A matter that is decided on, named by the domain. A Flow groups decisions by it.

A day for which the registration is read: "in force" is always in force on such a day. A fact, never the clock (rule 3), and itself a choice of the domain. The decision records are read as they stand on it.

slots.description: The day as people write it.
The day as the whole number YYYYMMDD (the stopgap of Decision.valid_from_day).

lines: // Rules of std-decision, in the Datalog subset, so Soufflé is the oracle.
// The base relations are the pack's tables: decision(d), decision__state(d, s), decision__supersedes(new, old),
// decision__decider(d, who), decision__valid_from_day(d, n), decision__valid_until_day(d, n),
// reference_date__day(r, n), and the two ends of a ground g: ground__decision(g, d) and ground__rests_on(g, d).
// A day is a whole number YYYYMMDD until rules read dates (schema/decision.yaml).
// Time comes from the validity days and from supersedes, never from the state: the state is what the record
// says today, and a reference date may lie before or after today. So a decision whose record says superseded
// is in force on a reference date before its successor took effect.
// replaces: the transitive closure of supersedes. a replaces b directly or through decisions in between.
.decl replaces(a: symbol, b: symbol)
replaces(a, b) :- decision__supersedes(a, b).
replaces(a, c) :- replaces(a, b), decision__supersedes(b, c).
// Axiom: supersedes has no cycle. No decision replaces itself.
// @invariant
.decl supersession_cycle(decision: symbol)
supersession_cycle(a) :- replaces(a, a).
// Axiom: a decision does not end on or before the day it starts.
// @invariant
.decl window_inverted(decision: symbol)
window_inverted(d) :- decision__valid_from_day(d, f), decision__valid_until_day(d, u), u <= f.
// took_effect: on reference date r, decision d has been taken and its first day f has come. The rule reads the
// decision itself, decision(d), so a proof that rests on a decision ends in its record.
.decl took_effect(decision: symbol, on: symbol)
took_effect(d, r) :- decision(d), reference_date__day(r, n), decision__valid_from_day(d, f), f <= n,
!decision__state(d, "proposed").
// ended: on reference date r, the last day of decision d has passed (valid_until u is the first day without it).
.decl ended(decision: symbol, on: symbol)
ended(d, r) :- reference_date__day(r, n), decision__valid_until_day(d, u), u <= n.
// replaced: on reference date r, decision s, which supersedes d, has taken effect. It stays so when s itself
// ends or is replaced later: a decision does not come back by itself.
.decl replaced(decision: symbol, by: symbol, on: symbol)
replaced(d, s, r) :- decision__supersedes(s, d), took_effect(s, r).
.decl was_replaced(decision: symbol, on: symbol)
was_replaced(d, r) :- replaced(d, _, r).
// in_force_on: decision d is in force on reference date r. It has taken effect, its last day has not passed,
// and no decision that supersedes it has taken effect.
.decl in_force_on(decision: symbol, on: symbol)
in_force_on(d, r) :- took_effect(d, r), !ended(d, r), !was_replaced(d, r).
.decl has_start(decision: symbol)
has_start(d) :- decision__valid_from_day(d, _).
// has_successor: a decision that has been taken and names its first day supersedes d.
.decl has_successor(decision: symbol)
has_successor(d) :- decision__supersedes(s, d), has_start(s), !decision__state(s, "proposed").
// Axiom: a superseded decision is not in force. From the day a successor takes effect that holds by the rule
// above. What is left is a record that says superseded while no decision that has been taken supersedes it:
// by the rules it is then in force on r, against its own record.
// @invariant
.decl superseded_in_force(decision: symbol, on: symbol)
superseded_in_force(d, r) :- decision__state(d, "superseded"), in_force_on(d, r), !has_successor(d).
.decl has_decider(decision: symbol)
has_decider(d) :- decision__decider(d, _).
// Finding: decision d is in force on r, and its record names nobody who took it. About the registration, not
// the world (decider is open): somebody decided, the record does not say who.
// @absence
.decl in_force_without_decider(decision: symbol, on: symbol)
in_force_without_decider(d, r) :- in_force_on(d, r), !has_decider(d).
// Finding: the record of d says in force and names no first day, so d is in force on no reference date.
.decl in_force_without_start(decision: symbol)
in_force_without_start(d) :- decision__state(d, "in_force"), !has_start(d).
// Finding: the record of d says withdrawn and names no first day. By its days d is in force on no reference
// date, and no day says when it stopped. A decision may still rest on d, and a rule that asks whether a ground
// still stands reads this relation, not the state.
.decl withdrawn_without_start(decision: symbol)
withdrawn_without_start(d) :- decision__state(d, "withdrawn"), !has_start(d).
// proposal: the record of d says proposed, so d has not been taken. A proposal names grounds as a decision
// does; a rule that reads grounds uses this relation to say which of the two it speaks of.
.decl proposal(decision: symbol)
proposal(d) :- decision__state(d, "proposed").
// ground_chain: the transitive closure of the grounds. a rests on b because the record of a names b as a ground,
// or through decisions in between. It is what the records name; whether any of them is in force is not in it.
.decl ground_chain(decision: symbol, rests_on: symbol)
ground_chain(a, b) :- ground__decision(g, a), ground__rests_on(g, b).
ground_chain(a, c) :- ground__decision(g, a), ground__rests_on(g, b), ground_chain(b, c).
// Axiom: the grounds have no cycle. No decision rests on itself.
// @invariant
.decl ground_cycle(decision: symbol)
ground_cycle(a) :- ground_chain(a, a).

.output replaces, supersession_cycle, window_inverted, took_effect, ended, replaced, in_force_on, superseded_in_force, in_force_without_decider, in_force_without_start, withdrawn_without_start, ground_cycle

module.description: The decision record. A decision is an origin of facts (S32, class decision): somebody decided it, on a day, and it applies from a day until it ends or a later decision supersedes it. A fact of a domain that is a decision points to a Decision with an arrow of its own; rules read whether that decision is in force on a reference date (rules/decision.dl). The fields follow MADR: title, status, deciders, date, supersedes. A decision may rest on other decisions (Ground) and may look at an earlier one again (reassesses).
